contradictions: SLOTS 55/56/60 — DuckObservation.swift:23,25 calls body x/y/yaw 'ALWAYS ZERO, unbound in training'. The training configs bound them: microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:682-687 samples all six body axes U(-0.005,0.005) m / U(-0.05,0.05) rad, and standup.py:632-637 keeps x/y at +/-0.005 m and yaw at +/-0.05 rad as deliberate untracked 'alive noise'. They are structurally exactly 0.0 only in sitstand/ground_pick/ball_kick/roulade, which pad the whole body block with mdp.zero_command_padding. AUTHORITATIVE FOR THIS TABLE: DuckKit. DuckObservation.build appends literal 0.0 at those three indices (lines 121, 122, 126 as of 2026-08-30; the entry said 95, 96, 100, which is where they were before the file grew) and DuckCommand has no x/y/yaw field at all, so no caller and no slider can move them for ANY policy. DuckKit's word 'unbound' is wrong, but its behaviour is safe: 0.0 is the distribution centre in walk/standup and the exact trained constant everywhere else.

SLOT 53 head_yaw travel — microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:663 justifies the +/-1.40 rad cap as 'limit +/-pi/2 with HOME=0'. Both copies of robot_walk.xml declare head_yaw range=-2.967059728390 2.967059728390 (+/-170 deg): microduck_rl-develop/src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/robot_walk.xml:203 and duckkit/Tests/DuckKitTests/Fixtures/duck/robot_walk.xml:58. AUTHORITATIVE: the XML — it is the model MuJoCo actually loads, and DuckModel.jointRanges:59 agrees with it to 1e-13. The shipped +/-1.40 command cap is unaffected and is more conservative than the comment implies (47% of real travel, not 89% of pi/2).

SLOT 51 neck_pitch reachability — microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:660-662 claims the per-joint final caps are 'XML limits minus HOME offset, with ~10% safety margin', giving neck_pitch +/-1.10. neck_pitch's XML range is ASYMMETRIC, (-1.5707963267948966, +1.0471975511965976) (robot_walk.xml:181; DuckModel.jointRanges:57), and HOME is +0.3491 (DuckModel.homePose:44), so the reachable delta is (-1.9199, +0.6981). A +1.10 command is 0.40 rad past the mechanical stop. AUTHORITATIVE: the XML. Editor consequence: slot 51's slider is honest as a *training range* but everything above +0.70 is trained-but-unreachable and will clamp at the joint limit. Slot 52 (head_pitch, symmetric +/-pi/2, reachable +1.2217) has no such problem.

SLOT 54 head_roll travel — microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:664 says 'head_roll: +/-0.31 rad (limit +/-20 deg)'. The XML limit is +/-0.4363 rad = +/-25 deg (robot_walk.xml:216; DuckModel.jointRanges:60). AUTHORITATIVE: the XML. The +/-0.31 cap is conservative under either reading, so only the comment is wrong.

ACTION SCALE — CORRECTED 2026-08-30. DuckModel.swift:103 sets actionScale = 0.9 and :106 standingActionScale = 1.0, but the per-policy value is DuckPolicyKind.actionScale (DuckModel.swift:217-222), which returns 1.0 for stand, sitStand, groundPick and roulade and 0.9 only for walking and the two kicks, mirroring robotd's per-network scales. Training sets joint_pos_action.scale = 1.0 (microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:273, overriding the mjlab base 0.5), and infer_policy.py's --action-scale default is 1.0. AUTHORITATIVE: the training config — the servo target formula must match what the policy was optimised against. Not an observation slot, but it means DuckKit drives walking and the two kicks at 90% of trained joint amplitude and everything else at 100%. WHAT THIS ENTRY USED TO SAY, and why it is worth recording: 'DuckModel.swift:88 sets actionScale = 0.9 for every policy except .stand … DuckKit drives every non-standing policy at 90% of trained joint amplitude'. DuckKit stopped doing that — its own comment at DuckModel.swift:208-216 records the fix and names the three it had wrong — so this entry was reporting a disagreement four policies larger than the one that exists, at a line number that had also moved.

ACTION FILTERING — RESOLVED 2026-08-30, and DuckKit is right. Fetched directly: pollen-robotics/microduck robotd/src/control.rs:68-81 declares head_lowpass: Option<f64> defaulting to Some(0.5) and legs_lowpass Some(0.7), applied at :439 and :444; deploy/robotd.toml:137-138 carries them commented out, so the defaults are what runs. SO THE ROBOT DOES FILTER. What is wrong is robotd's stated REASON: control.rs:498-505 labels them 'trained with ACTION_LOW_PASS_HEAD_ALPHA' / 'ACTION_LOW_PASS_LEG_ALPHA', and pollen-robotics/microduck_rl CLAUDE.md:67 states the opposite as a repo invariant — 'Policies are UNFILTERED (no action low-pass in training). Don't add EMA filtering without a matched runtime flag and a transfer test'. microduck_rl scripts/infer_policy.py:792-794 agrees: target_positions = default_pose + action * action_scale, no filter, only an optional delayed_action for latency. DuckModel.swift:110-129 already says exactly this and its rule — apply when modelling what robotd sends to servos, NEVER in a replay of what a policy did in simulation — is correct. NOTE the cited file moved: microduck_rl/AGENTS.md is now CLAUDE.md and 404s at main.

JOINT COUNT — DuckModel.jointNames:21-25 declares 15 joints with 'mouth' at index 9; both robot_walk.xml files declare exactly 14 hinge joints and no mouth. NOT A REAL CONFLICT: DuckModel.swift:50 is explicit that 'the fourteen policy joints carry the MuJoCo model's ranges; the mouth carries the runtime's -5..+30 deg', and DuckObservation.policyJoints drops index 9 via jointOfPolicySlot before the vector is built. The surviving 14 match robot_walk.xml declaration order (left leg 5, head chain 4, right leg 5) exactly, and DuckModel.homePose minus the mouth is byte-identical to infer_policy.py's DEFAULT_POSE. Both sources authoritative in their own domain.

symmetry.py:30-31 justifies the pitch-chain sign flips with 'left_hip_pitch = +0.6, right_hip_pitch = -0.6'. Actual HOME is left -0.4579 / right +0.4579 — opposite signs AND a different magnitude. AUTHORITATIVE: microduck_constants.py:84-85 and DuckModel.homePose:43-45, which agree with each other exactly. The mirroring logic symmetry.py describes is still correct; only its illustrative numbers are stale.

SLOT 50 yaw-rate range — infer_policy.py:964-969 caps the keyboard yaw command at +/-1.5 rad/s; training range is ang_vel_z (-1.0, 1.0) (microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:650) with no widening curriculum (:890 deletes it). AUTHORITATIVE FOR A SLIDER: the training range. The runtime cap runs 1.5x out of distribution and nothing in the obs pipeline clips it.

SLOTS 51-54 runtime head cap — infer_policy.py:357-359 applies one uniform +/-1.4 rad cap to all four head slots. Training caps are per-joint: 1.10 / 1.10 / 1.40 / 0.31 (microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py:826). AUTHORITATIVE: the per-joint training caps. The uniform runtime cap lets head_roll be driven 4.5x past anything it saw in training, which is why slot 54's slider must stay at +/-0.31.

BODY SUB-BLOCK ORDER — infer_policy.py:389-391 says 'body_cmd[0..2] currently mean (dz, dpitch, droll)'. DuckObservation.swift:24 explicitly contradicts it: 'body z, roll, pitch — in that order, not z, pitch, roll'. AUTHORITATIVE: DuckKit, corroborated twice — symmetry.py:18 gives [55:61] as (x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw), and standup.py:632-637 lists roll before pitch. The infer_policy docstring describes only the dead legacy 51-D path; DuckKit is right and slots 58/59 are roll then pitch.
unknowns: No training bound exists for base_ang_vel (slots 0-2). Every ObservationTermCfg in the env leaves clip=None and scale=None, so the gyro enters the net raw and unclipped; the only number attached to it is the Unoise +/-0.03 rad/s corruption. The +/-10 rad/s slider is an EDITOR CONVENTION, grounded only in DuckModel.rouladeDuration = 1.0 s for one full forward roll (2*pi rad/s ≈ 6.3 rad/s pitch rate, so +/-10 comfortably encloses the most violent shipped behaviour). It is not a trained range and must not be quoted as one.

No training bound and no actuator velocity limit exists for joint_vel (slots 20-33). microduck_constants.py's _BAM_ACTUATOR_KWARGS (lines 120-132) specifies only motor_name, model, target regex, kp_fw, vin_range, vin_drop_gain_range, vin_min and delay lags — there is no velocity_limit, effort_limit or speed field anywhere. The +/-5 rad/s slider is an EDITOR CONVENTION sized to enclose XL330 servo top speed at the 6.5-8.2 V bus range; it was NOT established from the repos. The one hard fact available is the corruption magnitude, Unoise +/-0.25 rad/s.

No bound exists for last_action (slots 34-47). The value is the raw pre-scale ONNX output, unclipped in training (no clip on the term) and unclipped in infer_policy (no clip_actions configured). The +/-3.0 slider is DERIVED, not read: the largest reachable joint delta from home is 2.0287 rad (left_hip_pitch), so at scale 1.0 an action of 2.03 already saturates the widest joint and +/-3.0 leaves headroom. Treat it as a display convention.

Which training env produced each of the seven policies DuckPolicyKind names (DuckModel.swift:194-201). DuckKit vendors ONE .onnx, alpha_walking, as a test fixture; the nine files in DuckStudio/Resources are the app's own copies, and two of them (roller, roller_crouch) have no DuckPolicyKind case at all, so this question is open for nine files and not seven. Checked 2026-08-30 — the old wording said 'the seven ONNX files DuckKit ships' at DuckModel.swift:147-155, and neither the count nor the line range was right. This determines the alwaysZero answer for slots 57/58/59: the body block is structurally exact 0.0 in sitstand/ground_pick/ball_kick/roulade (zero_command_padding), sampled-but-reward-weight-0.0 in the velocity env, and genuinely live only in standup (axis_weights (0,0,1,1,1,0)). No checkpoint-to-env manifest was found on this machine, so slots 57-59 are marked non-zero on the strength of the standup env alone. If alpha_stand did not come from standup.py, those three are dead too.

The PPO iteration count of each shipped checkpoint. The head-command training sigma differs by ~25x between curriculum stage 0 (neck/head pitch 0.0289) and the final stage 2000 (0.635), so slots 51-54 cannot be sensitivity-ranked or normalised without knowing which stage a checkpoint stopped at. The slider bounds above assume the FINAL stage; an earlier checkpoint would make the head slots as degenerate as the body slots.

rsl_rl's EmpiricalNormalization epsilon. Normalisation is baked inside the ONNX (export.py emits actor(normalizer(obs))), and rsl_rl is not vendored on this machine, so the effective divisor for the near-degenerate body slots — and therefore how far a small body command blows up after normalisation — cannot be quoted.

The mouth joint (DuckModel index 9, travel -5 deg to +30 deg) has NO observation slot. It is absent from both robot_walk.xml files and dropped by DuckObservation.policyJoints, so it cannot appear in a 61-slot editor at all. Any mouth control must be driven outside the policy contract.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT FILTER EXISTS UPSTREAM AND THIS PACKAGE DOES NOT MODEL IT. deploy/robotd.toml:36-41 documents a per-tick EMA on INCOMING COMMANDS — `cmd += alpha * (target - cmd)`, with cmd_alpha and head_alpha both 0.2, described as turning 'a stick snap into a ramp the gait can follow'. That is upstream of the policy, on the twist and head command, and is not the same thing as the action low-pass applied downstream of it. Nothing in DuckKit or StudioKit smooths a command, so a preview that steps a command instantly is unlike the robot in a way nobody here has measured. Found 2026-08-30 while closing the action-filter contradiction; not yet chased.
